_comment: What this harness assumes about Claude Code. upstream-check.sh compares these
assumptions against the installed CLI and fails when they stop being true.
acknowledged_hook_events is not 'events we use' — it is 'events a human has
looked at and made a decision about'. When upstream adds one, the check fails
until someone either hooks it or adds it here, which is the acknowledgement.
That is the mechanism that keeps the harness current instead of quietly stale.
acknowledged_surface does the same job for capabilities that are NOT hook
events: tools and settings keys. It exists because hook events were the only
thing the check could enumerate, so cross-session messaging — two tools and
two settings keys, shipped in 2.1.224 — landed while the check reported
'contract holds'. A checker's population is where things hide: anything
outside it reads as an all-clear.
READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING A GREEN RUN: acknowledged_surface is verified, not
discovered. `claude doctor` enumerates hook events, so section 4 can catch an
event nobody has seen. Nothing enumerates tools or settings keys, so section
4c can only confirm that what a human already wrote down still exists. A new
capability no one has noticed will not appear here on its own — that is a
standing limitation, and the check prints it rather than implying coverage.
Capability -> the decision a human made about it. Verified by substring
match against the CLI binary, which is advisory: a build could mangle a
string, so a miss is a prompt to check by hand, never a hard failure.

tools.SendMessage: Acknowledged 2026-08-27, not restricted. Cross-session messaging (2.1.224). Sends plain text to another of your sessions; it cannot approve a permission prompt or change config on the receiving side, so it does not widen this harness's blast radius. Deny it in permissions.deny to turn sending off.
tools.ListAgents: Acknowledged 2026-08-27, not restricted. Lists reachable sessions. Read-only, names and status only. Paired with SendMessage in any deny rule, since denying one without the other leaves a half-working surface.

settings_keys.crossSessionInbound: Acknowledged 2026-08-27, deliberately NOT set. With permissions.defaultMode 'auto' the receiving session counts as prompting, so inbound messages are delivered and a value would change nothing here. Left unset on purpose: an adopter running bypassPermissions gets holds instead, and that is the correct default for them. Revisit if this harness ever ships bypassPermissions.
settings_keys.isolatePeerMachines: Acknowledged 2026-08-27, deliberately NOT set. Requires approval before a message leaves the machine. Only meaningful with Remote Control connected, which this harness does not configure. Set it to true if this machine ever joins one.
settings_keys.dialogExpiry: Acknowledged 2026-08-27, deliberately NOT set. Governs how long a held inbound message waits for approval (default five minutes). The default is right for interactive use; a long-running `claude -p` worker wanting unattended delivery should set crossSessionInbound rather than stretch this.
settings_keys.subagentPromptCacheTtl: Acknowledged 2026-09-22, deliberately NOT set. Measured over 14 days of this machine's transcripts: main-session cache writes were all 1h (6,869), subagent writes all 5m (1,624). Only 4 of 1,614 subagent turns followed a gap over 5 minutes (303,618 tokens re-cached). Raising it would put every subagent write on the pricier 1h rate to save those 4. Revisit if the audit log's Agent lines show long-lived background subagents.
settings_keys.syncClaudeAiSkills: Set false 2026-09-24. The synced skills bucket on the owner's Mac was created 2026-09-17 (file birth time), so the evidence covers about 6 days: no call to any of the 8 synced skills in local transcripts since then, while the Skill tool was called 14 times over 30 days (61 transcript files), all to built-in skills. Their descriptions added 5,083 chars to every session (measured by the 2026-09-23 review). Synced skills can also carry inline shell commands that run under this machine's allow rules. They still work on claude.ai. Re-check if a synced skill is wanted in the terminal.
settings_keys.syncClaudeAiPlugins: Set false 2026-09-24 with syncClaudeAiSkills. The synced bucket held only a marketplaces file, so nothing is lost; it keeps a synced plugin, which could carry a function-hooks (Mods) module that sits above the classic guards, off this machine.
settings_keys.maxEffortLevel: Acknowledged 2026-09-22 (2.1.267), NOT set. Caps effort for every model and subagent. The harness ships effortLevel xhigh and has no measurement that a cap would save anything without costing quality; revisit with the audit log's Agent lines.
settings_keys.bashEditDiffEnabled: Acknowledged 2026-09-22 (2.1.269), NOT set. Adds a diff of files a Bash command changed to its result. Useful but grows every such tool result; left to the user.
settings_keys.attribution: Acknowledged 2026-09-23 (2.1.281), NOT set. `false` hides all commit and PR attribution. The harness wants the co-author line (includeCoAuthoredBy true), and older CLIs skip a settings file holding the boolean form.
settings_keys.maxProseWidth: Acknowledged 2026-09-25 (2.1.282), NOT set. Caps prose width in wide terminals; tables and code keep full width. A display preference, left to the user.
settings_keys.availableModelsMatch: Acknowledged 2026-09-25 (2.1.283), NOT set. Managed setting: with "exact", an availableModels entry allows only the model version it names, so a new release stays blocked until listed. The harness sets neither availableModels nor availableModelsMatch in config/settings.json; model allow/deny policy is the owner's call, not a harness guard.
settings_keys.deniedModels: Acknowledged 2026-09-25 (2.1.283), NOT set. Managed setting to block specific models even when availableModels allows them. Same reasoning as availableModelsMatch: the harness ships no model allow/deny list, so this is left unset for the owner to decide.
settings_keys.allowedProviders: Acknowledged 2026-09-29 (2.1.285), NOT set. Managed setting that limits which API providers a machine may use. Same reasoning as availableModelsMatch and deniedModels: provider policy is the owner's call, not a harness guard, and config/settings.json ships no managed policy.

notes_on_unused_events.PermissionRequest: STRONG candidate, payload confirmed 2026-09-09: receives tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id, permission_mode and effort, and returns {decision: allow|deny|ask, decisionReason}. With defaultMode auto the classifier resolves prompts a human used to see, so auditing its decisions would restore the lost record. Note the limitation: it fires where a permission DECISION is requested, so it is PermissionDenied below that carries the auto-mode denial.
notes_on_unused_events.PostCompact: Candidate: pre-compact.sh backs up the transcript; a post-compact counterpart could record what survived.
notes_on_unused_events.PermissionDenied: STRONGEST candidate, payload confirmed 2026-09-09: receives tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id, denial_reason and permission_mode, and returns {retry}. This is the one gap that bit during this review: a session hit a classifier denial and audit.log recorded the attempt but NOT the verdict, so the friction census had to be reconstructed by re-deriving the matcher's rules over 40,346 logged commands instead of just reading the denials. Hooking this makes that measurement a lookup. Caveat: denial_reason is reportedly the fixed string 'Blocked by classifier' rather than a detailed explanation, so it identifies WHICH command was denied, not why.
notes_on_unused_events.PreModelSwitch: Acknowledged 2026-09-09, not adopted. Appeared between 2.1.250 and 2.1.266. Fires before a model switch is applied and CAN block it, returning permissionDecision allow/deny plus a reason. Not hooked: this harness does not police which model runs, and gating the model picker would be friction with no security gain. Revisit if model choice ever becomes a cost or compliance control.
notes_on_unused_events.PostModelSwitch: ADOPTED 2026-09-09 (audit.sh). Fires after a model switch; cannot block, returns systemMessage/additionalContext only. This entry first read 'not hooked, because audit.sh already records the tool calls either side of a switch, so the change is visible in the log' -- that was wrong and is kept here as the correction: every audit line is <ts> | <tool> | <target> | <dir> with no model field, so a switch left no trace whatsoever. For a long background session producing analysis, an unrecorded fallback silently changes the reliability of everything after it.
notes_on_unused_events.SubagentStart: Not adopted: subagent activity is already visible via PostToolUse.
notes_on_unused_events.UserPromptSubmit: Not adopted deliberately: it sees every prompt, which is the most privacy-sensitive surface in the harness.
notes_on_unused_events.TaskCreated: Not adopted: background-task lifecycle is not a security or continuity concern.
notes_on_unused_events.Setup: Not adopted: install.sh already owns first-run setup.
notes_on_unused_events.TeammateIdle: Not applicable to a single-developer harness.
notes_on_unused_events.Elicitation: Not adopted: MCP elicitation is out of scope (MCP is an explicit known limitation).
notes_on_unused_events.PostToolBatch: Not adopted: audit.sh already logs each tool call individually.
notes_on_unused_events.StopFailure: Candidate: would catch a Stop hook erroring, which currently fails silently.
notes_on_unused_events.InstructionsLoaded: Not adopted: CLAUDE.md loading is not audited.
notes_on_unused_events.CwdChanged: Not adopted: audit.sh already records cwd per entry.
notes_on_unused_events.DirectoryAdded: Candidate: --add-dir widens the file surface the guards protect.
notes_on_unused_events.FileChanged: Not adopted: external file changes are not the harness's concern.

upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn._comment: Reviewed 2026-08-12. If the harness duplicates one of these, delete the harness copy rather than maintaining two.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.auto-mode classifier: Adjudicates the permission prompts the guards' ask tier used to send to a human. See README 'Auto mode'.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.autoMode.{allow,soft_deny,hard_deny,envi: Native rule layer. VERIFIED 2026-09-09, replacing an earlier guess that read 'appears to replace the shipped defaults': a category set WITHOUT the literal string "$defaults" in its array does replace the entire default list for that section -- for soft_deny that discards every built-in soft block including force push, curl-pipe-bash, production deploys and auto-mode bypass; for hard_deny it discards the built-in data-exfiltration rule. Including "$defaults" splices the defaults in at that position, so entries can go before or after them. The harness shipping none was therefore the right call, but the reason is now a fact with a documented escape hatch rather than an assumption, so adding entries is safe PROVIDED "$defaults" is always present. autoMode.environment is prose describing which repos, buckets and domains are trusted, and is the documented lever for reducing classifier denials -- preferred over widening permissions.allow, because the two are independent gates: permissions is consulted first, the classifier second.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.auto-dream memory consolidation: Background memory hygiene with its own lock and rollback. See docs/memory-hygiene-research.md — do not rebuild it.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.shared/team memory sync: Server-side concurrent-write rejection, mass-delete guard, and secret scanning on memory writes.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.sandbox: OS-level containment; the real boundary the regex guards only approximate.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.symlink-aware native permission rules: 2.1.268 applies deny/ask rules to a path's real location and 2.1.280 judges writes by where they land. Overlaps sensitive-file-guard's symlink resolution. Keep the guard: it also covers Grep and reads that no shipped deny rule names.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.per-command allowed_domains: 2.1.271, auto mode with sandboxing only. Overlaps network-guard's domain allowlist, but the harness ships sandbox.enabled false, so it does not apply here.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.Read/Edit deny on unanalyzable Bash line: Added in 2.1.268, REVERTED in 2.1.273: eval / env -C lines prompt again instead of being denied. The hole interpreter-guard and env-guard cover is open upstream; both stay.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.Artifact tool vs WebFetch rules: 2.1.268: WebFetch deny/ask rules no longer apply to Artifact reads and publishes, and network-guard is matched on WebFetch only. Audited, not guarded: audit.sh logs Artifact, ArtifactData and ArtifactComments calls (action, url, ids, never content). Decide on a guard from that census. 2.1.281: artifact pages may also load scripts from unpkg.com; same census.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.auto mode and skill inline ! commands: 2.1.271: a skill's or slash command's inline ! commands follow permission rules, not the classifier. The shipped allow list includes broad entries (Bash(python3:*), Bash(node:*)), so such a command matching them runs without classifier review. Open question for the owner.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.Claude in Chrome per-site check in auto: 2.1.275: classifier-approved browser calls skip the extension's per-site check. No harness guard covers browser tools; the MCP audit census records them.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.recursive rm prompts in auto mode: 2.1.281: rm whose target is only command-substitution output (rm -rf "$(pwd)") now asks even with a Bash allow rule, and in auto mode the dangerous-rm prompt denies after 2 minutes with a rewrite hint. The shipped deny Bash(rm -rf:*) already refuses the literal form. Both opt-outs (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_SUBSTITUTION_RM_PROMPT, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_DANGEROUS_RM_TIMEOUT) stay unset.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.server-side auto mode classifier: 2.1.281: where the classifier runs server-side, read-only and sandboxed shell commands also wait for it, and CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER now applies on a direct API connection. The PreToolUse guards run first either way. Not set.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.permission rules with a NUL byte: 2.1.281: such a rule now matches nothing instead of acting as a wildcard. No shipped rule has one.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.per-model effort on new models: 2.1.280: an effort level saved before /effort became per-model no longer applies to newly released models; they start at their default. Missed at the 2.1.280 review. Measured on this Mac 2026-09-23: Opus 5 messages ran xhigh, Opus 5.5 messages ran medium, despite effortLevel xhigh here. Fix per model with /effort; the status line now shows the live level.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.mid-pattern :* in Bash rules: 2.1.282: a rule with :* before the end of the pattern was skipped in settings files and now applies from every source. Checked 2026-09-25: no rule in config/settings.json or the installed ~/.claude/settings.json has one (grep -E ':\*[^)]' on each, 0 hits), so no rule starts matching. The deny rules spell a bare *, as in `git * push --force:*`, which this entry does not touch.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.Skill(claude-ai:*) allow rules: 2.1.282: now cover only skills synced from claude.ai. The harness ships no Skill() rule and sets syncClaudeAiSkills false, so nothing changes here.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.telemetry variables in project settings: 2.1.282: project and local settings may no longer turn telemetry export on, and a startup notice lists the ignored ones. The harness sets no telemetry variable in config/settings.json, and it writes user settings, which this does not affect.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.auto mode server-side classifier: 2.1.282: on a direct Anthropic API connection with telemetry off, auto mode now uses the server-side classifier (CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=0 opts out). This Mac signs in with a subscription and had DISABLE_TELEMETRY unset on 2026-09-25, so it is likely unaffected. Either way, a guard deny or ask applies before any classifier sees the call.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.auto mode when no permission mode is con: 2.1.283: an interactive session on a third-party provider, or with telemetry off, now starts in auto mode when nothing sets a permission mode, though permissions.defaultMode still overrides it. config/settings.json always sets permissions.defaultMode to "auto" explicitly, so this change cannot alter this harness's behavior either way.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT tool output loggin: 2.1.283: MCP tool, WebFetch and WebSearch outputs are added to the tool.output OpenTelemetry span event when OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT=1. Overlaps audit.sh, which already logs those same tool calls (action, target, dir) but deliberately never their content -- see the Artifact/WebFetch entry above for the same reasoning. config/settings.json sets no telemetry exporter and does not set OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT, so no tool content leaves this harness through OTel.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.sandboxed git credential helper store fi: 2.1.283: sandboxed git no longer asks credential helpers to store the sandbox proxy's login (which printed "failed to store"). config/settings.json ships sandbox.enabled false, so this harness never ran into the bug and the fix changes nothing here.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.managed sandbox settings fail closed on: 2.1.283: a managed sandbox block with one invalid nested value used to be ignored in its entirety; an invalid value now fails closed and the rest of the block still applies. Checked 2026-09-25: config/settings.json's sandbox block (enabled, failIfUnavailable, network.allowedDomains) has no invalid nested value, so nothing here newly fails closed -- but the change is a safety improvement for the day one does, since silent whole-block ignoring was the worse failure mode.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.Skill() deny rule matching for Desktop p: 2.1.283: Skill(anthropic-skills:<name>) deny rules now also block that skill when Claude Desktop delivers it as a plugin, and Skill(skill:<name>) denies now match the skill's alias and display name too. config/settings.json and rules/ ship no Skill() allow or deny rule, so this changes nothing here; revisit if one is ever added.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.auto mode read-outside-directory prompt: 2.1.284: the auto-mode prompt shown before a read outside the working directories gained a "Yes, but ask again next time" answer, so one read can be allowed while later ones still prompt. A UX addition to the same classifier prompt covered by 'auto-mode classifier' above; config/settings.json sets permissions.defaultMode auto and defines no autoMode.environment carve-out, so this changes only the prompt's answer choices, not this harness's exposure.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.auto mode when no permission mode is con: 2.1.284: widens the 2.1.283 change so interactive terminal and VS Code sessions start in auto mode when nothing sets a permission mode, on every plan and provider rather than only third-party providers or telemetry-off; permissions.defaultMode still overrides it. config/settings.json always sets permissions.defaultMode to "auto" explicitly, so this still cannot alter this harness's behavior.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.Ultracode decoupled from effort level: 2.1.284: Ultracode became its own toggle in /effort (Tab, or /effort ultracode [on|off]); it no longer forces xhigh effort and now stays on across every effort level instead of only at xhigh. The harness ships effortLevel xhigh (see maxEffortLevel above), set independently of Ultracode, so this doesn't change that setting -- but a session can now run Ultracode at a lower effort level than xhigh, where before enabling Ultracode implied xhigh. No harness action: the harness does not set or police the Ultracode toggle.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.external-imports approval for symlinked: 2.1.284: fixes rules symlinked into .claude/rules from outside the project being skipped without ever showing the external-imports approval prompt; a .claude directory symlinked in from outside the project now asks for the same approval. This harness's rules/ ships as regular files committed in-repo, not symlinked from elsewhere, so nothing here triggers the prompt either way; revisit if rules/ is ever consumed via a symlink.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.auto-memory loading neutralizes imperson: 2.1.284: MEMORY.md and recalled memory notes now have invisible characters and tags that imitate Claude Code's own markup neutralized before they reach Claude. Hardens the same MEMORY.md surface this harness's memory tooling (bin/memory-index.sh, bin/memory-verify.sh, bin/memory-fix.sh, hooks/memory-lint.sh) and the memory_index_limits entry below already work with; it reduces prompt-injection risk in memory content rather than overlapping a harness guard, so no harness change is needed.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.failed-hook stderr and exit code now log: 2.1.284: the debug log no longer drops a failed hook's stderr when the hook also wrote to stdout, and now logs a failed hook's exit status even when it produced no output at all. Improves diagnosability of this harness's own hooks/*.sh scripts (audit.sh and the guards) when they fail; no harness change needed, this is upstream debug-log fidelity only.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.Elicitation/ElicitationResult hook block: 2.1.284: {"decision":"block"} returned by an Elicitation or ElicitationResult hook now declines the MCP elicitation, matching what exit code 2 already did. This harness hooks neither event -- see notes_on_unused_events: 'MCP elicitation is out of scope' -- so the fix changes nothing here.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.SendMessage tool no longer advertised to: 2.1.284: sessions launched without the SendMessage tool, such as by Claude Desktop, are no longer told to message other sessions with it. Touches the same tool surface acknowledged as SendMessage/ListAgents above; this harness's sessions do carry SendMessage, so the fix doesn't change what they're told.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.sandboxed Bash startup fix for a write-d: 2.1.284: fixes sandboxed Bash commands failing to start on Linux when the working directory is write-denied and contains a read-denied directory. config/settings.json ships sandbox.enabled false, so this harness never hit the bug and the fix changes nothing here, the same reasoning as the 2.1.283 sandboxed git credential helper entry above.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.Sonnet 5.5 becomes the default Sonnet: 2.1.284: claude-sonnet-5-5 is now the default Sonnet on the Anthropic API. By 'per-model effort on new models' above, a newly released model starts at its default effort rather than the saved effortLevel xhigh, so a session or subagent that picks Sonnet will not run at xhigh until /effort is set for it. config/settings.json pins no model and this repo ships no agent that names Sonnet, so nothing here changes; check the status line's effort after the first Sonnet session.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.safety-related model switch target chose: 2.1.284: in sessions that pin Opus with ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL or modelOverrides, a safety-related switch now goes to the model the API picks for that flag, not the pinned model. config/settings.json sets neither, so this harness is unaffected; audit.sh already logs every PostModelSwitch as model_switch with from and to, so such a switch would show there either way. 2.1.287: the switch now keeps the current effort level instead of the new model's default, so it no longer falls through to the per-model default described in 'per-model effort on new models'.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.WebFetch can be turned off with CLAUDE_C: 2.1.285: a new environment variable removes the WebFetch tool entirely. Overlaps network-guard, which asks on WebFetch to a host outside its allowlist. config/settings.json does not set it, so WebFetch stays available and network-guard still applies; turning it off is the owner's call.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.ExitPlanMode hooks see the plan written: 2.1.285: PreToolUse hooks on ExitPlanMode could get a missing or outdated plan when the plan was written in the same response. hooks/plan-to-html.sh is such a hook and exits silently on an empty plan, so before 2.1.285 some plans likely rendered no HTML page or a stale one. The fix needs no harness change.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.synchronous hooks no longer hang on a ba: 2.1.285: a synchronous hook that starts a background process holding its output open no longer hangs Claude Code. No hook in hooks/ starts a background process (git grep for a trailing &, nohup or disown finds only guard patterns), so this harness was not exposed.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.cancelled shell command or hook no longe: 2.1.285: a Bash command or hook cancelled while it was being set up no longer starts and runs to its end. Upstream reliability fix; no harness change.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.Artifact allow rule no longer covers fil: 2.1.285: a 'don't ask again' Artifact allow rule stopped letting the tool publish a file outside the working directories without asking. Narrows the same surface as 'Artifact tool vs WebFetch rules' above; config/settings.json ships no Artifact allow rule and audit.sh still logs every publish.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.Auto-memory cannot be turned on from a b: 2.1.285: /memory can no longer turn Auto-memory on from a background session or one started by Claude Code's own tools; turning it off still works. Touches the memory surface the harness tooling manages, but the harness does not toggle Auto-memory, so no change.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.auto mode by default for claude -p on th: 2.1.285: extends 'auto mode when no permission mode is configured' to claude -p and the Python Agent SDK on third-party providers or with telemetry off. config/settings.json sets permissions.defaultMode auto explicitly, and the drift workflow runs first-party, so nothing here changes.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.project settings cannot widen an admin-r: 2.1.285: project settings can no longer widen or turn off an admin-required sandbox, or reopen managed read-denies; sandbox auto-allow also stopped asking on inline scripts that contain =. config/settings.json ships sandbox.enabled false and no managed sandbox, so neither changes anything here.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.per-turn performance with many deny rule: 2.1.285: faster turns when many permission deny rules and MCP tools are configured. config/settings.json ships 23 deny rules and no MCP servers, so any gain here is likely small; nothing to change.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.API 400 after a tool or hook returns a n: 2.1.286: fixes API 400 errors after a tool or hook returned an object, number or boolean instead of text. Every guard decision goes through emit_deny and emit_ask in hooks/lib.sh, which build permissionDecisionReason with jq --arg or a quoted printf, so the harness only ever returns strings; nothing to change.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.worktree subagents no longer load the pr: 2.1.286: subagents spawned with worktree isolation stopped loading the project CLAUDE.md and its imports a second time from the worktree copy. The harness ships no CLAUDE.md; install.sh copies its instructions into ~/.claude/rules, which is user scope and not in a worktree copy. Upstream context fix, no harness change.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.secret redaction in logs, transcripts an: 2.1.286: redaction now catches a secret whose key name hides an invisible character, and the /feedback transcript no longer holds invalid JSON lines after redaction. hooks/secret-scanner.sh guards what is written, not what Claude Code logs, so the two do not overlap; nothing to change.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.one retry limit per model call: 2.1.286: one retry limit now covers a whole model call, so with default retry settings a failing call sends at most 14 requests. config/settings.json sets no retry variables (grep -i retr finds none), so the default applies; nothing to change.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn./hooks opens on one list grouped by even: 2.1.286: /hooks now lists configured hooks grouped by event, one Enter to view a hook, plus wording and column changes. Display only; the hooks config/settings.json registers are unchanged.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.Claude Mods: plugins may modify deeper b: 2.1.287: plugins can now change deeper behavior, and a built-in mod (You should know) ships disabled. config/settings.json already sets syncClaudeAiPlugins false so a synced plugin carrying a Mods module cannot reach this machine (see that settings key above); nothing to change. Missed by the section 6 filter.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.dangerous rm keeps its always-ask safegu: 2.1.287: an rm on / or the home directory lost its always-ask safeguard when the same command redirected output to a ~ or wildcard path. config/settings.json denies Bash(rm -rf:*) and Bash(rm -rf /:*) regardless, so the harness backstop held for -rf; the upstream fix also covers forms those prefixes do not match. Missed by the section 6 filter.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.shell writes through a repo-committed sy: 2.1.287: a shell write through a symlink committed to the repo, onto a sensitive file or out of the working tree, now names where it lands and asks. Overlaps hooks/sensitive-file-guard.sh, which canonicalizes paths to defeat symlink bypass but only sees file-tool paths, not shell redirects; the upstream check covers the shell side. Keep both. Missed by the section 6 filter.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.whole-tool Bash allow rules and allowing: 2.1.287: a whole-tool Bash allow rule or a hook that allows no longer lets a shell write reach files the file tools refuse (profile store, host credentials). config/settings.json has no whole-tool Bash allow (every Bash allow is a prefix rule), and hooks/lib.sh emits only deny or ask, so no harness hook ever allows; nothing to change.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.asyncRewake hook with a missing script r: 2.1.287: an asyncRewake hook whose script is missing no longer wakes Claude repeatedly. No hook in config/settings.json uses asyncRewake; nothing to change.

_comment: The two thresholds that decide how much of MEMORY.md is loaded, read out of
the CLI rather than assumed. They were folklore here for a while: this repo's
own research doc recorded '~200-line index cap is unsubstantiated', while
memory-verify and memory-lint both enforced 200 as fact. Both turned out to
be right about the number and wrong about the confidence.
Upstream destructures {trimmed, lineCount, byteCount} and tests
lineCount > <lines> and byteCount > <bytes>. The size limit is BYTES -- the
identifier is literally byteCount -- which is why this harness reports bytes.
Truncation is line-first: the index is cut to <lines> lines, then clamped to
<bytes>, so passing line 200 drops everything after it.
Section 4d re-extracts both numbers by name, so a minifier rename cannot
strand the check the way a hardcoded identifier would.
